title: The Ray Beneath the Ledger
paras: At the entrance to the fictional Estuary Museum, a preserved ray hangs above a nineteenth-century harbour ledger. This exhibition follows the animal from the muddy [[quay|quay]] where it was landed to the cabinet where it became a scientific specimen. Together, these objects expose how a collector’s [[mania|mania]] for unusual creatures could obscure the people whose knowledge made discovery possible.

In the first gallery, visitors encounter the notebooks of naturalist Tomas Vale, alongside petitions from fishing families. Under the harbour concession, guards could [[restrain|restrain]] fishers who refused to surrender unusual catches. Such [[oppression|oppression]] supplied Vale’s collection at considerable human cost. One petition names net-maker Amara Sen as the families’ [[proxy|proxy]], authorised to negotiate compensation while they remained at sea.

The central display shifts attention to the ray itself. Its skeleton consists of [[cartilage|cartilage]], strong yet flexible tissue, with supporting elements extending into its broad fins. A shallow tank model helps visitors [[visualize|visualize]] its passage through suspended silt. Nearby, an empty preservation jar recalls another practical difficulty: the alcohol used to protect specimens was highly [[inflammable|inflammable]], requiring storage away from lamps.

The final cabinet places Vale’s published account beside the original ledger, whose payments reveal contributions his narrative omitted. Celebrating him as a solitary discoverer would therefore [[distort|distort]] the historical record. The museum has rewritten the specimen’s label with descendants of the fishing families. To [[embody|embody]] this shared approach, the label now includes extracts from the petitions alongside Vale’s description of the ray.
zh: 在虚构的河口博物馆入口处，一条保存下来的鳐鱼标本悬挂在一本十九世纪的港口账簿上方。本展览追溯了这条鱼从被卸上泥泞码头，到进入陈列柜成为科学标本的历程。这两件展品共同揭示：收藏家对奇异生物的狂热，如何可能掩盖那些凭借自身知识促成科学发现的人。
在第一展厅，参观者会看到博物学家托马斯·韦尔的笔记，以及渔民家庭提交的请愿书。依据港口特许经营规定，守卫可以限制拒绝交出罕见渔获的渔民的人身自由。这种压迫为韦尔的收藏提供了标本，却让渔民付出了沉重代价。其中一份请愿书指定织网匠阿玛拉·森为各家的代理人，授权阿玛拉在渔民出海期间协商补偿事宜。
中央展区将注意力转向鳐鱼本身。它的骨架由软骨这种坚韧而富有弹性的组织构成，支撑结构延伸到宽大的鳍中。一个浅水槽模型帮助参观者在脑海中描绘它穿过悬浮泥沙的情景。旁边的一只空标本保存罐则提醒人们注意另一项实际困难：用于保存标本的酒精极易燃烧，必须远离灯火存放。
最后一个陈列柜将韦尔发表的记述与原始账簿并置，账簿中的付款记录揭示了他在叙述中略去的他人贡献。因此，将他赞颂为独自完成发现的人，会歪曲历史记录。博物馆与渔民家庭的后人共同重写了标本说明。为了体现这种共同参与的做法，说明中如今既有请愿书的节选，也有韦尔对鳐鱼的描述。

q.s: Fishing families empowered Amara Sen to discuss compensation on their behalf during their absence at sea.
q.why: 第二段说明阿玛拉获授权在渔民出海时协商补偿。

q.s: The liquid used to preserve specimens could safely be kept beside burning lamps.
q.why: 第三段指出保存用酒精易燃，须远离灯火。

q.s: The fishing families’ descendants received payment for helping revise the specimen’s label.
q.why: 末段提到后人参与改写，未说明是否获报酬。
